Main.sentence: Sochi (Russian: Сочи , .mw-parser-output .IPA-label-small{font-size:85%}.mw-parser-output .references .IPA-label-small,.mw-parser-output .infobox .IPA-label-small,.mw-parser-output .navbox .IPA-label-small{font-size:100%} IPA: [ˈsotɕɪ] ⓘ , from ___E:Ubykh U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ubykh_language)___ : Шъуача – seaside ) is the largest ___E:resort city U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resort_town)___ in Russia.

The city is situated on the ___E:Sochi River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sochi_(river))___ , along the ___E:Black Sea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Sea)___ in the ___E:North Caucasus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Caucasus)___ of ___E:Southern Russia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Russia)___ , with a population of 466,078 residents,  and up to 600,000 residents in the urban area. The city covers an area of 176.77 square kilometers (68.25 sq mi),  while the Greater Sochi Area covers over 3,502 square kilometers (1,352 sq mi).

Sochi stretches across 145 kilometers (90 mi), and is the longest city in Europe,  the fifth-largest city in the ___E:Southern Federal District U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Federal_District)___ , the second-largest city in ___E:Krasnodar Krai U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krasnodar_Krai)___ , and the ___E:sixth-largest city U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Sea#Urban_areas)___ on the Black Sea.

Sochi hosted the ___E:XXII Olympic Winter Games U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Winter_Olympics)___ and ___E:XI Paralympic Winter Games U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Winter_Paralympics)___ in 2014. It hosted the alpine and Nordic Olympic events at the nearby ski resort of ___E:Rosa Khutor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosa_Khutor_Alpine_Resort)___ in ___E:Krasnaya Polyana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krasnaya_Polyana,_Sochi,_Krasnodar_Krai)___ .

It also hosted the Formula 1 ___E:Russian Grand Prix U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Grand_Prix)___ from 2014 until 2021.    It was also one of the host cities for the ___E:2018 FIFA World Cup U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup)___ .

The general consensus (also recognized by the city's own website  ) is that the name "Sochi" ( ___E:Russian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_language)___ : Сочи ) is the Russified form of the ___E:Circassian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circassian_languages)___ "Ş̂açə" ( ___E:Adyghe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adyghe_language)___ : Шъачэ ) which in turn is of ___E:Ubykh-Circassian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ubykh_language)___ origin, coming from the Ubykh name "Ş̂uaça" ( ___E:Ubykh U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ubykh_language)___ : Шъуача ).
It is a ___E:compound U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compound_(linguistics))___ made up from the two Ubykh words "шъуа" (sea) and "ча" (side) and roughly translates to "Seaside/coast".

There are other claims and theories, according to Georgian sources, the word comes from the Georgian word for the ___E:fir U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fir)___ tree, "soch'i" ( ___E:Georgian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgian_language)___ : სოჭი ).

___E:Colchis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colchis)___ 13th century BC–63 AD ___E:Achaemenid Empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achaemenid_Empire)___ 511 BC–330 BC ___E:Kingdom of Pontus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Pontus)___ 111 BC–62 BC ___E:Roman Empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Empire)___ 62 BC–337 AD ___E:Kingdom of Lazica U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Lazica)___ 337–697 ___E:Byzantine Empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Byzantine_Empire)___ 697–786 ___E:Kingdom of Abkhazia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Abkhazia)___ 778–1008 ___E:Kingdom of Georgia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Georgia)___ 1008–1490 ___E:Mongol Empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mongol_Empire)___ 1242–1259 ___E:Principality of Abkhazia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principality_of_Abkhazia)___ 1491–1829 ___E:Ottoman Empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottoman_Empire)___ 1578–1829 ___E:Circassia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circassia)___ 1829–1864 ___E:Russian Empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Empire)___ 1864–1917 ___E:Russian Republic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Republic)___ 1917–1918 ___E:Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Soviet_Federative_Socialist_Republic)___ 1918 ___E:Georgian Democratic Republic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgian_Democratic_Republic)___ 1918–1919 ___E:South Russia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Russia_(1919%E2%80%931920))___ 1919–1920 ___E:Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Soviet_Federative_Socialist_Republic)___ 1920–1991 ___E:Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Soviet_Federative_Socialist_Republic)___ 1922–1991 ___E:Russian Federation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Federation)___ 1991–present

Before the whole area was conquered by ___E:Cimmerian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cimmerian)___ , ___E:Scythian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scythian)___ and ___E:Sarmatian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarmatian)___ invaders, the ___E:Zygii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zygii)___ (Proto- ___E:Adyghe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circassians)___ ) people lived in ___E:Lesser Abkhazia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lesser_Abkhazia)___ under the ___E:Kingdom of Pontus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Pontus)___ , then the ___E:Roman Empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Empire)___ 's influence in ___E:antiquity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classical_antiquity)___ .

From the 6th to the 11th centuries, the area successively belonged to the Georgian kingdoms of ___E:Lazica U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lazica)___ and ___E:Abkhazia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Abkhazia)___ , who built a dozen churches within the city boundaries, the later was ___E:unified U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Georgia#Unification_of_the_Georgian_State)___ under the single ___E:Georgian monarchy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Georgia)___ in the 11th century, forming one of the ___E:Saeristavo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saeristavo)___ , known as ___E:Tskhumi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duchy_of_Tskhumi)___ extending its possessions up to ___E:Nicopsis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicopsis)___ .

The Christian settlements along the coast were destroyed by the invading ___E:Alans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alans)___ , ___E:Khazars U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khazars)___ , ___E:Mongols U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mongol_Empire)___ and other ___E:nomadic empires U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nomadic_empire)___ whose control of the region was slight.

The northern wall of an 11th-century ___E:Byzantine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Byzantine_architecture)___ ___E:basilica U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basilica)___ still stands in the ___E:Loo Microdistrict U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loo_Microdistrict)___ .

Between the ___E:13th U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/13th_century)___ and ___E:15th centuries U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15th_century)___ , the ___E:Republic of Genoa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_Genoa)___ had the monopoly of the trade on the shores of the Black Sea, and established colonies and trading posts in the region of the present-day Sochi, the large ones were ___E:Layso U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adler_Microdistrict)___ and ___E:Costa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khosta_Microdistrict)___ .

From the 14th to the 19th centuries, the region was dominated by the ___E:Abkhaz U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abkhaz_people)___ , ___E:Ubykh U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ubykh_people)___ , ___E:Abazin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abazins)___ and ___E:Adyghe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adyghe_people)___ tribes, the current location of the city of Sochi (Ş̂açə) known as ___E:Ubykhia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ubykhia)___ was part of historical ___E:Circassia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circassia)___ , and was controlled by the native people of the local mountaineer clans of the north-west Caucasus, nominally under the sovereignty of the ___E:Ottoman Empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottoman_Empire)___ , which was their principal trading partner in the Islamic world.

The coastline was occupied by Russia in 1829 as a result of the ___E:Russo-Circassian War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russo-Circassian_War)___ and the ___E:Russo-Turkish War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russo-Turkish_War_(1828%E2%80%931829))___ , 1828–1829; however, the ___E:Circassians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circassians)___ did not accept the Russian control over ___E:Circassia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circassia)___ and kept resisting the newly established Russian outposts along the ___E:Circassian coast U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circassian_coast)___ ( ___E:Adyghe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adyghe_language)___ : Адыгэ хы Iушъо ).

Provision of weapons and ammunition from abroad to the Circassians caused a diplomatic conflict between the ___E:Russian Empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Empire)___ and the ___E:British Empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britain%27s_Imperial_Century)___ that occurred in 1836 over the ___E:mission of the Vixen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mission_of_the_Vixen)___ .

The Russians had no detailed knowledge of the area until Baron ___E:Feodor Tornau U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Feodor_Tornau&action=edit&redlink=1)___ investigated the coastal route from ___E:Gelendzhik U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gelendzhik)___ to ___E:Gagra U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gagra)___ , and across the mountains to ___E:Kabarda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabarda)___ , in the 1830s. [citation needed] In 1838, the fort of Alexandria, renamed Navaginsky a year later, was founded at the mouth of the ___E:Sochi River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sochi_River)___ as part of the Black Sea coastal line, a chain of seventeen fortifications set up to protect the area from recurring Circassian resistance.

At the outbreak of the ___E:Crimean War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crimean_War)___ , the garrison was evacuated from Navaginsky to prevent its capture by the Turks, who effected a landing on ___E:Cape Adler U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adler,_Russia)___ soon after.

The last battle of the ___E:Russo-Circassian War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russo-Circassian_War)___ , the ___E:Battle of Qbaada U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Qbaada)___ , took place in 1864, and the Dakhovsky fort was established on the site of the Navaginsky fort. The end of the Caucasian War was proclaimed at Qbaada tract (modern ___E:Krasnaya Polyana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krasnaya_Polyana,_Sochi,_Krasnodar_Krai)___ ) on June 2 (21 May ___E:O.S. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Style)___ ), 1864, by the manifesto of ___E:Emperor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emperor)___ ___E:Alexander II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_II_of_Russia)___ , read aloud by ___E:Grand Duke Michael Nikolaevich of Russia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Duke_Michael_Nikolaevich_of_Russia)___ .
The city was the administrative capital of the ___E:Sochinsky Okrug U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sochinsky_Okrug)___ .

By the end of ___E:Russo-Circassian War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russo-Circassian_War)___ , the Russian Empire aimed to systematically destroy the native Circassian people in the region    and several atrocities were committed by the Russian forces.

As a result, almost all ___E:Ubykhs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ubykh_people)___ and a major part of the ___E:Circassians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circassians)___ who lived on the territory of modern Sochi, were either killed or expelled to the ___E:Ottoman Empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottoman_Empire)___ in the ___E:Circassian genocide U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circassian_genocide)___ .
According to Russian sources, Sochi's population fell from roughly 100,000, to 98.
Starting in 1866 the coast was actively colonized by Russians, Armenians, Ukrainians, Belarusians, Greeks, Germans, Georgians and other people from inner Russia.

Additionally in the late 1860s, the Adyghe, mostly of the ___E:Shapsug U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shapsugs)___ and Khakuchi tribes, who were hiding in the mountains started resettling on the coast.

In 1874–1891, the first ___E:Russian Orthodox church U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Orthodox_Church)___ , ___E:St. Michael's Church U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Michael%27s_Church,_Sochi)___ , was constructed, and the Dakhovsky settlement was renamed Dakhovsky ___E:Posad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Posad)___ on April 13, 1874 ( ___E:O.S. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Style)___ ).
In February 1890, the Sochi Lighthouse was constructed.

In 1896, the Dakhovsky ___E:Posad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Posad)___ was renamed Sochi ___E:Posad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Posad)___ (after the name of local river) and incorporated into the newly formed ___E:Black Sea Governorate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Sea_Governorate)___ .
In 1900–1910, Sochi burgeoned into a sea resort.
The first resort, "Kavkazskaya Riviera", opened on June 14, 1909 ( ___E:O.S. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Style)___ ).
Sochi was granted town status in 1917.

During the ___E:Russian Civil War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Civil_War)___ , the littoral area saw ___E:sporadic armed clashes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sochi_conflict)___ involving the ___E:Red Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Army)___ , ___E:White movement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_movement)___ forces, and the ___E:Democratic Republic of Georgia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Republic_of_Georgia)___ .
As a result of the war Sochi has become Russian territory.

In 1923, Sochi acquired one of its most distinctive features, a ___E:railway which runs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Caucasus_Railway)___ from ___E:Tuapse U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuapse)___ to Georgia within a kilometer or two of the coastline.

Although this branch of the ___E:Northern Caucasus Railway U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Caucasus_Railway)___ may appear somewhat incongruous in the setting of beaches and sanatoriums, it is still operational and vital to the region's transportation infrastructure.

Sochi was established as a fashionable resort area under ___E:Joseph Stalin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Stalin)___ , who had his favorite ___E:dacha U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dacha)___ built in the city. Stalin's study, complete with a wax statue of the leader, is now open to the public.

During Stalin's reign the coast became dotted with imposing ___E:Neoclassical U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoclassical_architecture)___ buildings, exemplified by the opulent Rodina and Ordzhonikidze sanatoriums.

The centerpiece of this early period is ___E:Shchusev U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexey_Shchusev)___ 's ___E:Constructivist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constructivist_architecture)___ Institute of Rheumatology (1927–1931).
The area was continuously developed until the demise of the Soviet Union.

Following Russia's loss of the traditionally popular resorts of the ___E:Crimean Peninsula U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crimean_Peninsula)___ ( ___E:transferred U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1954_transfer_of_Crimea)___ from the ___E:Russian SFSR U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_SFSR)___ to the ___E:Ukrainian SSR U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainian_SSR)___ in 1954 by ___E:Nikita Khrushchev U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev)___ ), Sochi emerged as the unofficial ___E:summer capital U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_capital)___ of the country.

In 1961, Soviet officials decided to expand the city limits by forming a Greater Sochi which extended for 140 kilometers from the southern parts of ___E:Tuapse U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuapse)___ to ___E:Adler U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adler_Microdistrict)___ .

In July 2005, Russia submitted a successful bid for hosting the ___E:2014 Winter Olympics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Winter_Olympics)___ in the city, spending around $51 billion in the process.

In 2019, an area in the ___E:Imereti Lowlands U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imereti_Lowlands)___ was separated from Adlersky city district to form a new ___E:urban-type settlement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban-type_settlement)___ named ___E:Sirius U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sirius_(urban-type_settlement))___ .
It was later designated as a ___E:federal territory U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federal_territory_(Russia)&action=edit&redlink=1)___ .
On January 11, 2025 there were 2 ___E:earthquakes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earthquake)___ in Sochi.
Greater Sochi is elongated along the Black Sea coast for 145 kilometers (90 mi).
Sochi is approximately 1,603 kilometers (996 mi) from ___E:Moscow U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow)___ .

The city of Sochi borders with ___E:Tuapsinsky District U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuapsinsky_District)___ in the northwest, with ___E:Apsheronsky District U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apsheronsky_District)___ and with ___E:Maykopsky District U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maykopsky_District)___ of the ___E:Republic of Adygea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adygea)___ in the north, with ___E:Mostovsky District U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mostovsky_District)___ in the northeast, and with ___E:Georgia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_(country))___ / ___E:Abkhazia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abkhazia)___ in the southeast.
From the southwest, it is bordered by the Black Sea.
The vast majority of the population of Sochi lives in a narrow strip along the coast and is organized in independent microdistricts (formerly settlements).

The biggest of these microdistricts, from the northwest to the southeast, are ___E:Lazarevskoye U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lazarevskoye_Microdistrict)___ , ___E:Loo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loo_Microdistrict)___ , ___E:Dagomys U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dagomys)___ , central Sochi ( ___E:Tsentralny city district U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tsentralny_city_district,_Sochi)___ ), ___E:Khosta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khosta_Microdistrict)___ , ___E:Matsesta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matsesta_Microdistrict)___ , and ___E:Adler U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adler_Microdistrict)___ .
The whole city is located on the slopes of the ___E:Western Caucasus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Caucasus)___ which descend to the Black Sea and are cut by the rivers.
The biggest rivers in Sochi are the ___E:Mzymta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mzymta_River)___ and the ___E:Shakhe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakhe_River)___ .
Other rivers include the Ashe, the Psezuapse, the ___E:Sochi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sochi_River)___ , the Khosta, and the ___E:Matsesta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matsesta_River)___ .
The ___E:Psou River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psou_River)___ makes the border with Abkhazia.

The northeastern part of the city belongs to the ___E:Caucasian Biosphere Reserve U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caucasian_Biosphere_Reserve)___ which is a ___E:World Heritage Site U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Heritage_Site)___ spanning areas in Krasnodar Krai and Adygea.

Almost the whole area of the Greater Sochi, with the exception of the coast and of the area which belong to the Caucasian Biosphere Reserve, are included into ___E:Sochi National Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sochi_National_Park)___ .

Sochi has a ___E:humid subtropical climate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humid_subtropical_climate)___   with mild winters (average 11 °C (52 °F) during the day and 4 °C (39 °F) at night) in the period from December to March and warm summers (average 24 °C (75 °F) during the day and 16 °C (61 °F) at night) in the period from May to October.
Sochi is unique among larger Russian cities as having some aspects of a ___E:subtropical U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subtropical)___ resort.

About two million people visited Greater Sochi each summer as of 2014,  when the city is home to the annual film festival " ___E:Kinotavr U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinotavr)___ " and a getaway for Russia's elite.

A ___E:UNESCO U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNESCO)___ ___E:World Heritage Site U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Heritage_Site)___ , the 2,957 square kilometers (731,000 acres) ___E:Caucasus Nature Reserve U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caucasus_Nature_Reserve)___ , lies just north from the city.  Sochi also has the region's most northerly ___E:tea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tea)___ ___E:plantations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plantation)___ .

Sochi has a ___E:humid subtropical climate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humid_subtropical_climate)___ ( ___E:Köppen climate classification U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification)___ Cfa ),  at the lower elevations.
Its average annual temperature is 18.9 °C (66.0 °F) during the day and 11.5 °C (52.7 °F) at night.
In the coldest months—January and February—the average temperature is about 10 °C (50 °F) during the day, above 3 °C (37 °F) at night and the average sea temperature is about 9 °C (48 °F).

In the warmest months—July and August—the temperature typically ranges from 25 to 29 °C (77 to 84 °F) during the day, about 20 °C (68 °F) at night and the average sea temperature is about 23–27 °C (73–81 °F).
Yearly sunshine hours are around 2,200. Generally, the summer season lasts three months, from June to September.
Two months—April and November—are transitional; sometimes temperatures reach 20 °C (68 °F), with an average temperature of around 16 °C (61 °F) during the day and 9 °C (48 °F) at night.
December, January, February and March are the coldest months, with an average temperature (for these four months) of 11 °C (52 °F) during the day and 4 °C (39 °F) at night.
Average annual ___E:precipitation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Precipitation_(meteorology))___ is about 1,700 millimeters (67 in).

Sochi is situated on the same latitude as ___E:Nice U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nice)___ but strong cold winds from the south make winters less warm. In fact, temperatures drop below freezing every winter.

The highest temperature recorded was 39.4 °C (102.9 °F), on July 30, 2000, and the lowest temperature recorded was −13.4 °C (7.9 °F) on January 25, 1892.  Sochi lies at 8b/9a ___E:hardiness zone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardiness_zone)___ , so the city supports different types of palm trees.

Within the ___E:framework of administrative divisions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subdivisions_of_Russia#Administrative_divisions)___ , it is, together with one ___E:urban-type settlement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban-type_settlement)___ ( ___E:Krasnaya Polyana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krasnaya_Polyana,_Sochi,_Krasnodar_Krai)___ ) and seventy-nine ___E:rural localities U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Types_of_inhabited_localities_in_Russia)___ , incorporated as the City of Sochi —an administrative unit with the status equal to that of the ___E:districts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Administrative_divisions_of_Krasnodar_Krai)___ .
As a ___E:municipal division U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subdivisions_of_Russia#Municipal_divisions)___ , the City of Sochi is incorporated as Sochi Urban Okrug .

Sochi is administratively subdivided into four city districts: ___E:Tsentralny city district U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tsentralny_city_district,_Sochi)___ , ___E:Lazarevsky city district U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lazarevsky_city_district)___ , ___E:Khostinsky city district U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khostinsky_city_district)___ , and ___E:Adlersky city district U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adlersky_city_district)___ .

Tsentralny city district, comprising the central portion of, is by far the smallest out of four in terms of the area, and the other three have comparable areas, with Lazarevsky city district being the biggest.
In terms of the population, Tsentralny city district is approximately twice as big as each of the other three city districts.

___E:Tsentralny city district U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tsentralny_city_district,_Sochi)___ , or central Sochi, covers an area of 32 square kilometers (12 sq mi) and, as of the ___E:2010 Census U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Census_(2010))___ , has a population of 137,677.  The highlights include:
___E:Lazarevsky city district U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lazarevsky_city_district)___ lies to the northwest from the city center; the 2010 Census showed the population of 63,894 people.
It is the largest city district by area, covering some 1,744 square kilometers (673 sq mi) and comprising several ___E:microdistricts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microdistrict)___ :

___E:Khostinsky city district U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khostinsky_city_district)___ , sprawling to the southeast from the city center, occupies approximately 374 square kilometers (144 sq mi), with a population of 65,229 as of the 2010 Census.
The district is traversed by many rivulets which give their names to the microdistricts of Matsesta ("flame-colored river"), Kudepsta, and Khosta ("the river of boars").

___E:Adlersky city district U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adlersky_city_district)___ , with an area of 1,352 square kilometers (522 sq mi) and a population of 76,534 people as of the 2010 Census,  is the southernmost district of the city, located just north of the border with Abkhazia.

Until the establishment of Greater Sochi in 1961, it was administered as a separate town, which had its origin in an ancient ___E:Sadz U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sadz)___ village and a medieval ___E:Genoese U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_Genoa)___ trading post.
Among the natural wonders of the district is the Akhshtyr Gorge with a 160-meter-long cave that contains traces of human habitation.

The upland part of the district includes a network of remote mountain villages ( ___E:auls U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aul)___ ), the ___E:Estonian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estonia)___ colony at ___E:Estosadok U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estosadok)___ , and the ski resort of ___E:Krasnaya Polyana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krasnaya_Polyana,_Sochi,_Krasnodar_Krai)___ which hosted the events (Alpine and Nordic) of the ___E:2014 Winter Olympics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Winter_Olympics)___ .
Also located here is a ___E:trout U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trout)___ fishery and a breeding nursery for ___E:great apes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_ape)___ .
Sochi has an ethnic ___E:Russian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russians)___ majority (~70%).

The city is home to a sizable ___E:Armenian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armenians_in_Russia)___ minority (~20%), which is especially notable in the ___E:Adlersky City District U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adlersky_City_District)___ where they compose more than half of the total population.

Most of Sochi's Armenian community are descendants of ___E:Hamshen Armenians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemshin_peoples)___ from Turkey's northeastern ___E:Black Sea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Sea)___ coast, who began arriving in the late 19th century.

The rest are ___E:Armenians from Georgia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armenians_in_Georgia)___ (particularly from ___E:Abkhazia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armenians_in_Abkhazia)___ and ___E:Samtskhe-Javakheti U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armenians_in_Samtskhe-Javakheti)___ ) and Armenia (especially from ___E:Shirak Province U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shirak_Province)___ due to the ___E:1988 earthquake U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Armenian_earthquake)___ ).

The ___E:Byzantine Empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Byzantine_Empire)___ brought Christianity to the Sochi region in the ___E:Middle Ages U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Ages)___ . [citation needed] The region was relatively isolated before 1829. [citation needed] In the North, a few hundred Sunni Muslim ___E:Shapsugs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shapsugs)___ , a part of the ___E:Circassian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circassians)___ nation, lived around Tkhagapsh, near ___E:Lazarevskoye U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lazarevskoye_Microdistrict)___ .
The Circassians (also known as Adyghe) converted to ___E:Islam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam)___ from Christianity in the 17th century.
In the nineteenth century, Islam spread to the region. [citation needed]

Currently, Sochi is a large predominantly ___E:Christian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christians)___ city, though there are thought to be around 20,000 Muslims (5% of inhabitants) living there now (the majority are ___E:Adyghe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adyghe_people)___ ) plus other Eastern ___E:Caucasians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peoples_of_the_Caucasus)___ , Turks, ___E:Tatars U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tatars)___ , and other smaller Muslim groups.

A ___E:mosque U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mosque)___ was built in 2008 by ___E:United Arab Emirates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates)___ in the central area of Bytkha, in addition to the old mosque being around 40 km (25 miles) north of the city center   in the Adyghe aul of Tkhagapsh.

There are around thirty ___E:Russian Orthodox U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Orthodox_Church)___ churches, the largest being St. Michael's, and two monasteries, plus two ___E:Catholic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Catholic_Church)___ churches, one in the center of Sochi and the other in Lazarevskoye.
The ___E:Armenian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armenia)___ community gathers in about ten churches.
Sochi is an economic centre of ___E:Krasnodar Krai U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krasnodar_Krai)___ and Russia.

According to the economist-geographer ___E:Natalia Zubarevich U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natalia_Zubarevich)___ , Sochi, being a "recreational capital", along with the largest industrial centers, acts as a "motor" of development that determines the prospects and directions of the country's development.
The economy of Sochi is based on trade, construction, resort and tourism.
Its structure for 2015: retail trade (59%), construction (15%), resorts and tourism (11%), industry (10.6%), transport (3.5%) and agriculture (0.9%).
Sochi is one of the most popular tourism centres, as well as a prominent financial centre in Russia.
Investments in the city's economy over the past 10 years have amounted to more than 1.1 trillion rubles.
The turnover of medium and large enterprises in Sochi in 2017 amounted to more than 191.3 billion rubles.
The increase in turnover in comparison with the previous year is 12%.

In 2010, Sochi headed the "Rating of Russian cities by quality of life" of the Urbanika Institute,  and in 2014 and 2015 it ranked as 4th and 5th city respectively;   experts noted the high rate of development of the city, large-scale investments on the eve of the ___E:2014 Winter Olympics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Winter_Olympics)___ , favorable environmental conditions and high safety of residents.
In 2012, Sochi topped the rating of "30 best cities for business" in Russia, by ___E:Forbes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes)___ .

Today, 705 classified accommodation facilities operate on its territory, including: 66 sanatoriums, 20 boarding houses and recreation centers and 618 hotels. 183 beach areas have been opened, more than 100 tourist facilities operate, about 70 excursion companies operate.
Over 5.2 million tourists visited Sochi in 2016, 5.9% more than in 2015.  The average annual occupancy rate of hotels was at 77%, but varies by season.
The importance of tourism for the development of Sochi is also determined by the financial revenues from the industry.
According to statistics, in 2015, tourism revenues amounted to about 30 billion rubles.
At the same time, throughout the country, revenues from the industry amounted to 161 billion rubles; thus, the tourist industry of the city occupies 18.6% of the total market of the country.
The retail trade turnover for medium and large enterprises (accounting for about 30% of the total turnover) in the city in 2016 amounted to 57.2 billion rubles.

On the territory of the city there are 8,769 objects of the consumer sphere, of which: 5013 are stationary retail enterprises, 1450 are catering enterprises, 335 are wholesale enterprises, and 1083 are service enterprises.
In Sochi, 1807 grocery stores, 2,708 non-food stores, 294 stores of a mixed group of goods, 178 pharmacies, 16 car dealerships, 20 stores at gas stations, 945 pavilions and kiosks have been opened.
The provision of the population with retail space is 1,106.7 m 2 (11,912 sq ft) per 1000 people.
According to 2017 data, the annual trade turnover per capita in Sochi was 1.75 times higher than the average in Russia (373,527 rubles per year per person).

At the same time, it exceeds the annual trade turnover per capita in all cities with a population of over one million, including ___E:Saint Petersburg U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Petersburg)___ and Moscow.
A high trade turnover is ensured by both a large flow of tourists and a high average wage in the city. The annual retail turnover generated by permanent residents is about 96.2 billion rubles (52%).
Tourists generate about 87.83 billion rubles (48%).

The turnover of public catering in the city in 2016 for medium and large enterprises amounted to 7 billion rubles (about 36% of the total turnover). 1450 public catering establishments were opened in Sochi, with a total of 90473 seats.
The market of paid services to the population in 2016 amounted to 34.3 million rubles; the industry employs 3393 people, with a total of 1083 enterprises.
The volume of goods shipped in 2016 for medium and large industrial enterprises of the city amounted to 19.4 billion rubles.

The distribution of energy, gas and water accounted for 11.9 billion rubles,  the largest enterprises in the industry are: Adler TPP and Sochinskaya TPP. Processing industries accounted for 3.3 billion rubles.
The volume of shipment of minerals amounted to 76 million rubles, the largest enterprise in the industry is Firma Sochinerud.
In the manufacturing industry, the overwhelming share of food production enterprises, which account for 92.3% of the production volume.
Large enterprises: Sochi meat-packing plant, Trout-breeding farm, Primorskaya quail farm, Sochi bakery and Lazarevsky bakery.
The volume of shipped agricultural products in 2016 amounted to 49.8 million rubles.
Vegetables, citrus fruits, fruits (including heat-loving crops such as feijoa, medlar, kiwi) and flowers are cultivated by large agricultural enterprises: Verlioka, Voskhod and Pobeda.
The only producer of poultry meat is the Adler Poultry Factory.
Five enterprises are engaged in the cultivation and processing of tea: Dagomyschay, Solokhaul tea, Matsesta tea, Khosta tea, Shapsug tea and a number of farmers.

A local ___E:tennis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennis)___ school spawned the careers of such players as ___E:Grand Slam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Slam_(tennis))___ champions ___E:Maria Sharapova U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maria_Sharapova)___ and ___E:Yevgeny Kafelnikov U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yevgeny_Kafelnikov)___ (Kafelnikov spent much of his childhood here, while Sharapova relocated to ___E:Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida)___ at the age of seven).

In late 2005, the ___E:Russian Football Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Football_Union)___ announced that it was planning to establish a year-round training center for the country's national teams in Sochi.
The city's warm climate was cited as one of the main incentives.

Sochi is also the home for the football team ___E:PFC Sochi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PFC_Sochi)___ which plays in the ___E:Russian Premier League U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Premier_League)___ and for the ice hockey team ___E:HC Sochi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HC_Sochi)___ which plays in the ___E:Kontinental Hockey League U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kontinental_Hockey_League)___ .

The nearby ski resort of ___E:Roza Khutor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosa_Khutor_Alpine_Resort)___ at ___E:Krasnaya Polyana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krasnaya_Polyana,_Sochi,_Krasnodar_Krai)___ was the location of the alpine and Nordic events for the ___E:2014 Winter Olympics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Winter_Olympics)___ .

In June 2006, the ___E:International Olympic Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee)___ announced that Sochi had been selected as a finalist city to host the ___E:2014 Winter Olympics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Winter_Olympics)___ and the ___E:2014 Winter Paralympics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Winter_Paralympics)___ .

On July 4, 2007, Sochi was announced as the host city of the 2014 Winter Games, edging out ___E:Pyeongchang U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyeongchang_County)___ , ___E:South Korea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korea)___ and ___E:Salzburg U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salzburg)___ , ___E:Austria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austria)___ .
This was Russia's first time hosting the Winter Olympic Games, and its first time hosting the Paralympic Games.
The site of a training centre for aspiring Olympic athletes, in 2008, the city had no world-class level athletic facilities fit for international competition.

Severe cost overruns made the 2014 Winter Olympics the most ___E:expensive Olympics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cost_of_the_Olympic_Games)___ in history; with Russian politician ___E:Boris Nemtsov U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Nemtsov)___ citing allegations of corruption among government officials,  and Allison Stewart of the ___E:Saïd Business School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sa%C3%AFd_Business_School)___ at ___E:Oxford U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Oxford)___ citing tight relationships between the government and construction firms.

While originally budgeted at US$12 billion, various factors caused the budget to expand to US$51 billion, surpassing the estimated $44 billion cost of the ___E:2008 Summer Olympics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics)___ in Beijing.

According to a report by the ___E:European Bank for Reconstruction and Development U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Bank_for_Reconstruction_and_Development)___ , this cost will not boost Russia's national economy, but may attract business to Sochi and the southern Krasnodar region of Russia in the future as a result of improved services.

The 2014 Winter Olympics in Sochi saw ___E:concern and controversy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concerns_and_controversies_at_the_2014_Winter_Olympics)___ following a new federal law approved in Russia in June 2013 that bans " ___E:homosexual propaganda to minors U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBT_rights_in_Russia)___ ".
There were also concerns over ___E:Islamist militants U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_terrorism)___ .

The state-controlled ___E:RAO UES U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RAO_UES)___ announced in July 2007 that it might spend 30 billion roubles (about US$1.2 billion) on upgrading the electrical power system in the Sochi area by 2014.  The power generating companies ___E:Inter RAO UES U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter_RAO_UES)___ and ___E:RusHydro U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RusHydro)___ would have to build or modernize four thermal power plants and four hydroelectric plants—and the federal grid company ___E:FGC UES U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FGC_UES)___ has to replace the Central-Shepsi electricity transmission line, which reportedly often fails in bad weather.

The new power line would run partly on power towers and partly across the bottom of the Black Sea. By 2011, the power supply of the resort area would increase by 1129 MW—of which 300 MW would be used for Olympic sports facilities. "The cost of the work is estimated at 83.6 billion rubles (about US $3.26 billion), of which 50 billion rubles (about US$2 billion) will go to investments in the electricity grid," the power companies announced.

They did not say how much of the bill the state would foot. In February 2007, when UES had planned to spend 48.8 billion rubles (about US$1.9 billion) on the Sochi area, the share the state had been ready to pay 38 billion roubles (about US$1.48 billion) of that.

The ___E:Silk Way Rally U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silk_Way_Rally)___ which is part of ___E:Dakar series U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dakar_Rally)___ took place in Sochi in 2010 for the last stage between the capital of the ___E:Republic of Adygea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_Adygea)___ ___E:Maykop U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maykop)___ to the city of Sochi through ___E:Pseshwap U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lazarevskoye_Microdistrict)___ .

President ___E:Vladimir Putin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Putin)___ had reached a deal with ___E:Bernie Ecclestone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernie_Ecclestone)___ for the city to host the ___E:Formula One U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One)___ ___E:Russian Grand Prix U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Grand_Prix)___ from 2014.  However, because of the ___E:2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine)___ , Sochi is not allowed to host future races.

The ___E:World Robot Olympiad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Robot_Olympiad)___ took place in the ___E:Adler Arena Skating Center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adler_Arena_Skating_Center)___ on November 21–23, 2014.

The ___E:2014 World Chess Championship U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_World_Chess_Championship)___ between ___E:Viswanathan Anand U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viswanathan_Anand)___ and ___E:Magnus Carlsen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnus_Carlsen)___ was played in Sochi in November 2014, with Carlsen emerging as the winner.

The ___E:Fisht Olympic Stadium U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fisht_Olympic_Stadium)___ was also used to host ___E:2018 FIFA World Cup U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_FIFA_World_Cup)___ ___E:football U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football)___ matches.

Public transport is represented mainly by bus and taxi. Sochi is served by the ___E:Adler-Sochi International Airport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adler-Sochi_International_Airport)___ .
